thread.title: Why this high-flying Dow stock looks ready to sputter - MarketWatch

author: Victor Reklaitis
title: Why this high-flying Dow stock looks ready to sputter - MarketWatch
text:
There’s more juice for the bulls, thanks to Apple’s tax-and-jobs splash that helped bring us Dow 26K.
While a government shutdown might kill the euphoric mood, for now even bitcoin is finding its feet a bit after staggering about for days.
But it’s Boeing BA, -2.90% that has really led the way to that Dow milestone . And so it is the target of our call of the day , which comes from several chart watchers, who say it’s time to sell or even bet against the soaring stock.
The trader with the Twitter handle “50 Pips” says wait for a crack and don’t short quite yet while sharing this Boeing chart:
presented without commentary > $BA pic.twitter.com/EJyOewUJMo
— 50 Pips (@50Pips) January 18, 2018 Others say the plane maker’s stock has partied too hard and climbed too far above its 50-day moving average, a closely watched level.
Cornerstone Macro’s Carter Braxton Worth has been looking at Boeing and Caterpillar CAT, +0.31% , another Dow component that has surged. Investors might want to take some profits on “ CatBo ” and even get short in the near term, the technical analyst suggests.
“They’re probably going to correct and perhaps in a meaningful way,” Worth tells CNBC .
The bearish chatter comes as Boeing’s stock shows a 19% gain so far this year, after its leap of about 90% in 2017 — and as the aerospace giant generates all sorts of headlines.
The Chicago-based company has jumped into the business of making airplane seats , plus it’s working with SpaceX and boarding the blockchain bandwagon . Analysts have been scrambling to raise their price targets , and the CEO for rival Airbus has blasted Boeing for “ ruthlessly surfing on this ‘America-first’ wave.”
There is no sign of Boeing losing altitude so far this morning, as the stock edges higher in premarket trading.
Read more: Boeing’s stock surges to another record
Key market gauges Futures for the Dow YMH8, -0.19% , S&P 500 ESH8, +0.02% and Nasdaq-100 NQH8, +0.13% are little changed. That’s after the Dow DJIA, -0.24% , S&P SPX, -0.04% and Nasdaq Composite COMP, +0.09% rose to fresh all-time highs yesterday, with blue chips closing above 26,000 for the first time .
The yield on the benchmark 10-year U.S. Treasury note has jumped above 2.6% for the first time since March.
Europe SXXP, +0.19% and Asia have been mixed. Gold GCG8, -0.82% is lower , while the dollar DXY, -0.50% edges up and oil CLG8, -0.11% is little changed.
See the Market Snapshot column for the latest action.
The chart Could bitcoin’s BTCUSD, +4.34% big selloff be winding down ? So far today the world’s No. 1 cryptocurrency is staying above yesterday’s low around $9,450, though it remains way below its mid-December high above $19,000.
See: How trading bitcoin could actually ruin your mental health
The buzz President Trump is denying that he changed his mind on a border wall, after White House Chief of Staff John Kelly suggested that Trump’s thinking had “ evolved .”
Apple AAPL, +0.25% says it will invest $350 billion in the U.S. economy and create 20,000 jobs , and CNBC’s Jim Cramer has cheered the effort as a “ modern-day Marshall Plan .” But does the announcement pass a sniff test ?
Days Inn parent Wyndham WYN, +4.99% plans to pay $1.95 billion for La Quinta’s LQ, +4.03% hotel business.
Morgan Stanley MS, +0.79% , BB&T BBT, +1.49% and GNC GNC, +50.00% are among the companies that have posted earnings before the opening bell.
On the economic front, readings on jobless claims and housing starts hit ahead of the open, then the Philly Fed index comes once trading is underway.
